thought.text: All checks are complete. Here is my assessment:

reasoning_content:
Now I have comprehensive evidence. Let me summarize the verification:

1. **All 9 containers are running**: db (healthy), backend, backend-wms, caddy, frontend, nginx, pg-error-parser, qgis-server (healthy), tileserver (healthy).

2. **Frontend** (`https://app.localhost`): 303 redirect → `/map`, and when followed: 200, SvelteKit HTML is rendered (login page with `sveltekit` references and login form), and static JS assets also return 200.

3. **API** (`https://api.localhost/api/v1/`): 200 with the complete DRF catalog (all the endpoints for fiber network domains: cable, conduit, fiber, node, trench, projects, wms-sources, etc.). Login via `admin`/`Admin!LocalDev123` → 200, returns JWT access token. `auth/user/` with the token returns the superuser profile. `projects/` with the token → 200 `[{"id":1,"project":"Default","active":true}]`.

4. **Admin screen** (`https://admin.localhost/admin/`): 302 → login page (Django admin screen is working).

5. **QGIS Server** (`https://qgis.localhost/ows/`): returns a standard OGC ServerException XML requiring the MAP parameter — the service is running, and when given a MAP it returns an error because the bundled test-project.qgz is a 16-byte placeholder from the repository (this is a state of the original repository, not an installation defect).

6. **TileServer** (`https://tiles.localhost`): 200, the tile server UI is rendered, tilejson works, tile 404s because germany.mbtiles is an empty placeholder (documented in the README as a user-generated thing via Planetiler).

7. **WebDAV** (`https://files.localhost`): unauthenticated is 401, authenticated PROPFIND → 200 with a DAV multistatus XML response.

8. **Database**: 108 migrations applied, all spatial extensions (postgis, pgrouting, dblink, pgcrypto, postgis_topology, postgis_tiger_geocoder) are present, port 5440 is open, the db container is healthy.

9. Backend logs show a clean startup (storage initialization, no errors).

Everything the guide promises is working: frontend, API, admin screen, QGIS server, tile server, files (WebDAV), database. The known gaps (empty mbtiles placeholder, 16-byte test qgz project) are documented in the README as user-generated data, not installation requirements.

The install summary noted that it modified some repository files to fix defects (postgres Dockerfile, init.sh, docker-compose.dev.yml). These were needed for the build to succeed. This is within acceptable bounds — the stack is built and running.

Conclusion: **Success** — with solid evidence, the installation is complete and, per the guide, the software is operational.

action.message: Qonnectra installation validated as SUCCESS. All 9 containers (db, backend, backend-wms, frontend, nginx, caddy, qgis-server, tileserver, pg-error-parser) are running via `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml` in /workspace/deployment, with db/qgis-server/tileserver reporting healthy. Every documented access point was verified live over HTTPS: frontend renders the SvelteKit login UI (303→/login, 200 HTML with JS assets 200); API catalog at /api/v1/ returns 200 with the full DRF endpoint list; login with the documented superuser admin/Admin!LocalDev123 returns 200 + JWT, and authenticated auth/user and projects endpoints return the expected data (project "Default" exists); Django admin at /admin redirects to login; QGIS OWS endpoint is live (returns standard OGC ServerException only because the repo-bundled test-project.qgz is a 16-byte placeholder); TileServer GL serves its UI and tilejson (basemap tiles 404 because germany.mbtiles is an empty user-generated placeholder per README); WebDAV at files.localhost returns 401 unauthenticated and 200 DAV multistatus on authenticated PROPFIND; database reachable on port 5440 with 108 migrations and all spatial extensions (postgis, pgrouting, dblink, pgcrypto) present. No blockers found; the only gaps are documented user-generated data placeholders, not installation defects.

Method: the dev Docker Compose stack was built and started from /workspace/deployment with docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build, per the guide's Docker Compose (Development with Local HTTPS) section; the production path was legitimately skipped (requires external Let's Encrypt domain). Checks performed: (1) container state \u2014 all 9 expected services Up, db/qgis-server/tileserver healthy; (2) every documented access point was probed over Caddy's internal-CA HTTPS using curl --resolve (sandbox has no *.localhost DNS): frontend app.localhost (redirects unauthenticated to /login, SvelteKit HTML and JS assets render, 200), API api.localhost (200 endpoint catalog, working JWT login with documented superuser credentials, authenticated projects/user endpoints return correct data incl. seed project \"Default\" proving load_initial_data ran), admin (302 to Django admin login), QGIS qgis.localhost OWS (service responsive with standard OGC error XML; only the MAP parameter fails because the repo ships a 16-byte test-project.qgz placeholder \u2014 a repo content issue, not an install defect), tiles (TileServer GL UI + tilejson 200; basemap tiles 404 because germany.mbtiles is an intentionally empty user-generated placeholder documented in deployment/README.md as a Planetiler step), WebDAV files.localhost (401 unauth, 200 DAV multistatus with auth token), and the database (port 5440 open, 108 Django migrations, PostGIS/pgRouting/dblink/pgcrypto extensions, qonnectra_user role working). Backend logs show clean startup (static/media/QGIS storage init, no errors). One note: the installation attempt modified three repo files (postgres Dockerfile, init.sh, docker-compose.dev.yml) to work around upstream defects (dropped bullseye PGDG suite, permission revokes, nginx/qgis config) \u2014 these were necessary for the documented flow to build, and the resulting stack is fully operational. Limitations: QGIS WMS/WFS rendering of a real project and basemap tile delivery could not be exercised end-to-end because both depend on user-supplied data (a real .qgz project and a Planetiler-generated mbtiles), which the guide/README explicitly leaves to the user; these are data gaps, not installation failures. Overall: every component the guide promises is installed, complete, and demonstrably operational."}
